text:
ConocoPhillips was essentially flat today, down just 0.02%, even as oil prices remain elevated: US crude at $107.89 and global Brent crude at $115.22. The stock has surged 8.5% over the past two weeks, riding a wave of geopolitical tension in the Middle East and energy supply disruption elsewhere—Iran tensions, Houthi strikes, and Ukrainian drone damage to Russian refining capacity have all pushed crude prices higher, which typically boosts an oil major's profits and stock price.

Today's tiny decline likely reflects profit-taking after that sharp two-week run-up rather than any new negative catalyst. The underlying conditions that drove the rally—Middle East conflict risk and global supply concerns—remain in place, leaving the stock near its recent highs with little clear reason to fall sharply.
